title: Raptors vs. Nuggets Post-Game Stats: Denver Escapes With Tight Win After Brandon Ingram's Late Three Falls Short - NewsBreak
text:
By Shabiha Akter ,
1 hours ago
Peyton Watson (Image Credits: Imagn) The Denver Nuggets took the floor for their first game of the season without Nikola Jokic, who is expected to miss a minimum of four weeks after suffering a hyperextended left knee . Playing without their MVP centerpiece, Denver found things difficult against the Toronto Raptors. However, Peyton Watson and Jamal Murray rose to the occasion with standout performances.
Wednesday night’s closing moments delivered high drama. With Denver holding a three-point lead, Bruce Brown missed both free throws that opened the door for Toronto. Brandon Ingram then drilled what appeared to be a game-tying three-pointer, but the shot was waved off after the buzzer sounded.
The basket didn’t count, ending Toronto’s hopes of forcing overtime. It allowed the Nuggets to narrowly escape with a 106–103 victory. The defeat dropped the Raptors to a 20–15 record on the season, while the Nuggets improved to 23–10 despite being shorthanded.
Peyton Watson and Jamal Murray Lead Shorthanded Nuggets Past Raptors Peyton Watson and Jamal Murray (Photo By Imagn Images) Watson delivered one of his most impressive outings of the season. He finished with 24 points and eight rebounds. He added two steals while shooting 9-of-19 from the field and converting 5-of-7 attempts from the free-throw line in 36 minutes of action.
Murray chipped in 21 points, seven rebounds, and six assists while knocking down six field goals, including two from beyond the arc. Jonas Valanciunas recorded 17 points, nine rebounds, and four assists in 23 minutes. He also contributed defensively with three blocks.
Jaden Pickett scored 10 points with two three-pointers, while DaRon Holmes II added 11 points, three rebounds, and a block. Bruce Brown finished with eight points and seven rebounds, though his missed free throws late nearly proved costly.
For Toronto, Brandon Ingram led all scorers with 30 points, eight rebounds, and five made three-pointers. Scottie Barnes added 20 points, 14 rebounds, and 10 assists.
Immanuel Quickley added 22 points and four assists, and RJ Barrett contributed 17 points while RJ Barrett had 17 points in the loss. Despite strong individual performances, Toronto fell just short in the final seconds of the game.
